(1) Fos immunoreactivities in the POA were distributed differently in NREM sleep, REM sleep and quiet and alert wake states; (2) a selective increase of Fos immunopositive neurons was found in the MnPN during NREM sleep; and (3) the SCN may be involved in the regulation or modulation of NREM sleep.
the MnPN is the only subregion of the POA activated during NREM sleep, and that the SCN is also activated during NREM, but not REM, sleep.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the neuronal activity of the POA during different behavioral states.
the neuronal circuitry of the POA involved in the generation of NREM sleep, and provides new information regarding the role of this brain region in the regulation of the sleep-wake cycle.
the identification of specific neuronal populations in the POA that may participate in the generation of NREM sleep, and the elucidation of the neuronal circuitry involved in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the POA is not a homogeneous region but rather is composed of functionally distinct subregions that may play a specific role in sleep-wake regulation.
the neuronal activation pattern of the entire POA is not state-specific but is regionally-specific.
the POA is not a homogeneous region but rather a complex network of neuronal groups that are activated differentially depending on the behavioral state of the animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

NREM sleep is associated with an increase in Fos immunoreactivities in the rostral portion of the SCN, MnPN, and in the VLPO, whereas the MnPN is the only POA region that shows a state-dependent increase in Fos during REM sleep induced by carbachol.
the neuronal network regulating NREM sleep is not restricted to a few discrete nuclei, but is dispersed throughout the POA.

the neuronal network controlling NREM sleep is distributed throughout the POA.
Fos immunoreaction is not a marker of REM sleep, as previously suggested.
the POA contains a heterogeneous population of neurons, which may be involved in different behavioral states.
